focus: Inbound subject capture — Channel#send_message_to_company and Channel#send_message_to_candidate
summary: All 7 tests passed. Both Channel#send_message_to_company and Channel#send_message_to_candidate correctly capture email.subject into the created channel_message.subject field. Nil subjects, empty string subjects, long subjects (254 chars), and subjects with special characters are all handled correctly.

methodology.approach: Rails runner script in RAILS_ENV=test against the messaging-improvements worktree
methodology.seed_pattern: Cypress-style seeding (User.first_or_create, Organization.first_or_create, job.candidates.build) with paid subscription enabled
methodology.email_mock: Ruby Struct responding to .subject, .body, .raw_html (matching the interface expected by Channel model methods)

code_under_test.mechanism: Both methods call channel_messages.build({...subject: email.subject...}) then save, passing the email's subject directly to the channel_message

tests.name: send_message_to_company with special chars in subject
tests.input_subject: Re: Fwd: Application for Senior Dev - resume and cover letter
tests.stored_subject: Re: Fwd: Application for Senior Dev - resume and cover letter

notes: send_message_to_candidate expects a User object as sender (not OrganizationUser), because it accesses sender.id and sender.organization_user_id — the latter is a method defined on User (line 252) that delegates to current_organization_user.id
send_message_to_company expects a Candidate object as sender, using sender.id as candidate_id
The CustomChannelMessageValidator on :subject only checks for {{placeholder}} patterns and does not block nil or empty subjects
The subject column is a VARCHAR (t.string) with no NOT NULL constraint, so nil is stored as NULL in the database
